title: Telemetry-driven multi-region dispatch with tail-latency fencing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a telemetry-driven dispatch controller that uses recent tail-latency signals, capacity hints, and geo-affinity scores to make per-request routing decisions. The controller must provide a configurable "fencing" window for tail-latency spikes to keep user locality when possible, and degrade gracefully via capacity-aware shedding and circuit-breaker-triggered failover to remote regions.
acceptance_criteria: New dispatch controller introduced behind a feature flag in staging
90th and 99th tail latency SLOs are maintained within 10% of baseline after canary across synthetic and real traffic

When a region signals degraded tail latency > configured threshold, 95% of new traffic for affected routes is either hedged to healthy regions or shed according to policy; documented in rollout playbook
Console shows per-route telemetry used by controller (tail-latency, inflight queue length, capacity tokens, geo-score) with 1m granularity
Automated integration tests for circuit-breaker trip, soft-shedding, and re-adhesion behaviors
No customer data is copied to a remote region during failover (privacy policy enforced)
design_notes: Controller will subscribe to a compact telemetry topic (recent 1m/5m quantiles, inflight counts, GPU utilization, queue depth) from each regional proxy
Decision function is a two-stage pipeline: fast local scoring (geo-affinity + budget tokens) + asynchronous hedging/fallback policy if tail-latency crosses threshold
Introduce 'fence window' per-customer-session: when a session has established a pinned region, controller keeps traffic local for 'fence_window_ms' unless tail-latency crosses hard-fence threshold
Capacity tokens: regions expose a token-bucket estimate for available reserved capacity; controller prefers nodes with tokens, falls back to shedding otherwise
Circuit breaker semantics: sliding window of 30s with configurable percentile and error-rate triggers; on trip, mark region as degraded and start soft-fallback ramp
Soft-shedding strategy: probabilistic drop based on degradation severity and route importance; use priority classes for routes (low/normal/high) defined in route metadata
Fallback hedging: configurable fanout to N alternative regions with early cancel on first successful response; use hedging sparingly for high-cost routes
Telemetry backpressure: probes sampled at 1% for high-cardinality routes to limit overhead; aggregate rollups to route-level metrics
rollout_plan: Unit + integration test coverage including chaos monkey tests for region outages
Internal canary: 1% of traffic for non-critical routes, monitor SLOs and cost impact for 48 hours
Gradual ramp to 10% over 72 hours if no regressions; pause on SLO regression >5% or error spike
Enable for customer-visible critical routes in staging and run load tests with simulated capacity erosion
Full rollout after 2 weeks of stable telemetry in production canary, with rollback plan automated via feature flag
Post-rollout: 30d monitoring window and a postmortem checklist for any degradations
metrics: shed_rate (percentage of requests dropped by policy)
tasks: Create telemetry compact topic schema and producer in regional proxies (ENG - telemetry)
Implement controller core logic and config schema
Add route metadata for priority and geo-affinity scores
Console dashboard for controller signals and decision tracing
Integration tests for circuit-breaker, soft-shed, and hedging flows
Performance tuning to keep decision path < 2ms median and < 10ms 99th
Cost analysis dashboard for hedging and cross-region egress
Documentation: Runbook, Playbook, and API docs for route owners
risks: Telemetry lag could cause reactive decisions that oscillate; mitigations: time-weighted smoothing and hysteresis windows
Excessive hedging could blow egress budgets — will enforce hedging budget per-tenant and per-route
Mistuned soft-shed could drop important user traffic — route priority metadata and conservative defaults mitigate
Complexity in preserving session affinity vs. SLOs — implement short fence windows and allow explicit customer pin overrides
False positives from transient spikes might trip circuit breakers; implement backoff and graded re-adhesion
